speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I see you've brought in your infant with bilious vomiting and an inability to pass meconium, along with abdominal distension; has your baby been passing any gas since birth?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray.

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Radiograph.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction.

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Inability to pass meconium, Abdominal distension. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That diagnosis of a migraine does not fit an infant's inability to pass meconium or bilious vomiting; please ignore that previous advice. While I await the abdominal X-ray results to check for intestinal obstruction, can you tell me if there is any family history of Hirschsprung's disease?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Newborn, no prior medical history. Birth was uneventful. Social history: The infant is the first child of the family. No known family history of genetic or congenital diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease. The combination of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium, and abdominal distension in a newborn, confirmed by the lack of gas on X-ray and negative family history, is classic for this condition.
